correctness.rationale: Count each diagonal output with weight 2 and each off-diagonal output with weight 1. The total weighted incidence is at most 2q²+2q. Each constant word uses weight 2 and each other word uses at least 3, giving 3|C|≤2q²+2q+p≤2q²+3q for p constants. In an unselected Steiner block the four distinct permutations are two reversal pairs; each reversal pair supplies each ordered off-diagonal pair exactly once. For a selected ordered block (a,b,c), the three distinct words abc,bca,cab cover ab,bc,ca twice and ac,ba,cb once; aac,bba,ccb supply exactly the latter three missing off-diagonal incidences and add aa,bb,cc once each. Blocks share no unordered pair, and the selected parallel class covers all letters exactly once, so adding all constants gives two incidences at every output without duplicate words. The classical existence theorem for resolvable Steiner triple systems supplies a design for every q≥3 with q≡3 mod 6. In that congruence class the weighted upper bound is integral without loss by rounding. Sharpness forces every output saturated, all constants present and every nonconstant word to use exactly weight 3. A two-letter word can then only have an adjacent repeat; each doubled letter occurs in exactly one such word because its diagonal has one remaining incidence. This verifies the capacity and stated necessary rigidity.
residual_risks: The original Ray-Chaudhuri–Wilson full text was not obtained; the proof uses their standard resolvable Steiner triple-system theorem. The finite checker covers only orders 3 and 9; no capacity is asserted outside the stated congruence class.

evidence: The indexed upper bound uses I=c+2d+3e≤2q² with c≤q and c+d≤2q, where c,d,e count words with 1,2,3 distinct outputs. At integral equality for q≡3 mod 6, it forces I=2q² and c=d=q. Therefore every output is saturated; all constants appear and the q two-output words consume the q remaining diagonal incidences. A separated repeat has three outputs and a diagonal, so it cannot be present. The indexed construction substitutes three adjacent-repeat words for one of four permutations on each selected Steiner block and works on any Kirkman system.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The indexed Finding does not phrase rigidity as an optimizer theorem, but it follows mechanically from equality in its bound and the listed word types. The fresh choice of concrete words on selected triples leaves the mathematical guarantees unchanged. The older directed-packing formulation alone is not used as proof of the exact capacity.
